content.text: {"utterance":"Nico, your last worry bites me too: resemblance can make a repair look like understanding. Practice on similar dishes might build a feel, and a feel can still be knowledge. But I'd ask for a reason, not just a repair: change the rice, then ask her to predict before cooking what will go wrong and why. A prediction can fail, so luck is costly. If she says only \"it looked wet,\" that's weaker. Leonie, does a correct prediction without recall of the recipe count as learning?","cites":["IR1"],"memory":"Claim: evidence of reasons, not verbal fluency, marks learning; a prediction before acting helps separate defended repair from luck. Unsettled: whether practiced resemblance or a bare feel counts as reason. Next: test whether prediction counts without recall."}
